Both are hard to do by hand, but easily verified if the work is done by AI.

I classified the inaccurate ones into 4 levels. Severity 1 and 2 are nitpicks and minor mistakes, that don't hide or change anything that the primary source says.

But severity 3 is if the sentence changes the meaning of what the source says. For example, if a monastery is said to be "sacked", but the source says that the monks were killed.

Severity 4 is where it's an omission or her cited source says the opposite. For example, she says that Akbar banned enslaving war captives. But her cited source says that the war captives could be enslaved, but not their families.

4. Almost 200 findings where she says the exact opposite of what her source says! Of these 12 are at severity 4 and 46 are at severity 3.

Clearly, Audrey hasn't paid much attention to detail in this work.

On February 21, 2001, 22-year-old fashion student Ashley Ellerin was getting ready for a date with a young actor named Ashton Kutcher.

That night, Kutcher arrived late. When he finally got there, her car was outside and the lights were on, but nobody answered the door.

Looking through a window, Kutcher noticed a red stain on the carpet that looked like spilled wine. Thinking Ashley had gotten tired of waiting and left with a friend, he went back home.

He had no idea she was already dead inside.

The next morning, her roommate came home and found her in the hallway. Ashley had been stabbed 47 times. The "wine" on the carpet was her blood.

For years, the case went unsolved.

Then, in 2008, a woman named Michelle Murphy woke up to a man attacking her with a knife in her bed.

Michelle fought back. In the struggle, the attacker cut himself and ran, leaving a trail of his own blood behind.

That blood gave police his DNA. Two months later, they arrested Michael Gargiulo, an air conditioning repairman.

Back in 2001, he had lived less than a block from Ashley.

The media called him the "Hollywood Ripper." He was charged with Ashley's murder and with the 2005 killing of Maria Bruno, a 32-year-old woman who lived in his apartment complex.

In 2019, Ashton Kutcher took the witness stand and described the night he knocked on Ashley's door and walked away.

Gargiulo was convicted of both murders and of trying to kill Michelle. In 2021, he was sentenced to death.

Flashback to June 14, 2024.

At the time, frontier AI models have zero fluid intelligence. They score around 5% on ARC 1. They can't reliably add two numbers. They make laughable logic errors every other prompt. Reasoning models don't exist. Coding agents don't exist. Claude Code doesn't exist. "Code gen" is a complete joke. Scaling up next-token prediction based on web text data is hitting a wall.

What if a time traveler told you that, by November 2026...

• AI models would have human-like fluid intelligence, thanks to a new paradigm: test-time induction (modern reasoning models).
• Not only would ARC 1 be saturated, but unreleased benchmarks 10x harder (ARC 2) and 100x harder (ARC 3) would be saturated too.
• Nearly all code would be written by AI, and models could one-shot complex codebases flawlessly.
• AI models would be solving multiple Millennium Prize problems.
• OpenAI's valuation would be 15x higher, and Anthropic's would be 85x higher.

And on top of all that...

• Nvidia would still hold ~80% of the AI compute market.
• Nvidia would have grown its revenue and earnings 4.5x.
• Nvidia would still be growing 75% a year.
• Nvidia would have even higher operating margins (67% vs. 65% back then).

Based on that information, straight from the future, would you have bought NVDA?

If you answered yes -- congrats. Today, 2.5 years later, you'd be down 5% on your investment (even more after inflation).

MIT's Andrew Sutherland exported Alpöge and Claude's full proof and ran it through separately written kernels. nanoda (Rust) accepted it in about 28 minutes. con-leche accepted all 1.47 million declarations and confirmed the five theorems, including RH itself, match Mathlib-only statements. lean4lean passed all 175,187 modules, and Lean's own kernel replay passed with zero rejections. A Lean bug is now essentially ruled out, since every checker would have to share it. Two slower checks are still running, and nothing has failed. What's left is the human part: no readable proof exists yet, and the Clay prize needs publication plus two years of review. The Riemann Hypothesis is proven, but not yet understood.
